articles.title: Name the Feeling and It Gets Smaller
articles.titleHinglish: Feeling Ko Naam Do, Wo Chhoti Ho Jaayegi
articles.content:
Most people have three words for their inner life: fine, stressed, and angry. That vocabulary is too small for the job, and the result is that everything uncomfortable arrives as one large undifferentiated weight.

There is a real difference between being angry and being humiliated. Between anxious and overwhelmed. Between sad and disappointed. Not a poetic difference — a practical one, because each points at a different action. Humiliation asks you to look at who was watching. Overwhelm asks you to cut the list. Disappointment asks you to look at what you had expected and whether it was ever agreed.

When you cannot tell them apart, you treat all of them the same way: distraction, snapping at whoever is nearest, or scrolling until it goes numb.

The practice is simple and takes about a minute. When something hits, say to yourself precisely what it is. Not I feel bad, but: I am embarrassed that I was corrected in front of the team, and underneath it I am afraid they think I am careless. That second half is where the actual information usually is.

Why does this help? Partly because a specific feeling can be addressed and a vague one cannot. And partly because the act of putting language on an emotion changes your relationship to it — you move from being inside the feeling to describing it, and description creates a small, useful distance.

A few things that make it easier.

Look for the second feeling. Anger is often the outer layer. Underneath is usually hurt, fear, or shame, which are harder to admit and more accurate. If you only ever treat the anger, you keep solving the wrong problem.

Locate it in the body. Tight chest, hot face, heavy shoulders, a stomach that will not settle. The body often knows before the mind agrees, and it is a faster way in.

Write one line, not an essay. The journal that helps is not the one where you explain yourself for two pages. It is the one where you write today I was more irritated than the situation deserved, and I think it was about the meeting.

And let the naming be the whole aim. This is not a technique for making feelings disappear. Some are supposed to stay for a while — grief does not want a solution, it wants room. What naming does is stop feelings from running the day from behind a curtain, which is the version that costs the most.
articles.contentHinglish:
Zyadatar logon ke paas apne andar ke liye teen shabd hote hain: theek hoon, stress hai, gussa aa raha hai. Yeh shabdkosh kaam ke liye bahut chhota hai, aur nateeja yeh hai ki har uncomfortable cheez ek bade bina shakal ke bojh ki tarah aati hai.

Gusse aur apmaan mein asli farq hai. Anxious aur overwhelmed mein. Udaas aur nirash mein. Yeh kavita wala farq nahi, practical farq hai, kyunki har ek alag kaam ki taraf ishaara karta hai. Apmaan poochhta hai — dekh raha kaun tha. Overwhelm kehta hai — list kaato. Niraasha poochhti hai — ummeed kya thi, aur kya kabhi wo tay bhi hui thi.

Jab aap inme farq nahi kar paate, to sabka ek hi ilaaj karte ho: dhyan hataana, jo paas mein ho uspar bhadak jaana, ya tab tak scroll karna jab tak sunn na ho jaaye.

Practice simple hai aur ek minute ki hai. Jab kuch lage, khud ko theek theek bolo ki hai kya. "Bura lag raha hai" nahi, balki: mujhe sharm aayi ki poori team ke saamne tokа gaya, aur uske neeche dar hai ki wo mujhe laparwaah samajhte honge. Asli information aksar us doosre hisse mein hoti hai.

Yeh madad kyun karta hai? Kuch isliye ki specific feeling ka kuch kiya ja sakta hai, dhundhli ka nahi. Aur kuch isliye ki emotion par bhasha rakhne se usse aapka rishta badal jaata hai — aap feeling ke andar hone se uska varnan karne par aa jaate ho, aur varnan thodi si, kaam ki doori bana deta hai.

Kuch cheezein jo aasaan bana deti hain.

Doosri feeling dhoondho. Gussa aksar bahar ki parat hai. Neeche aksar chot, dar ya sharm hoti hai — jinhe maanna mushkil hai aur jo zyada sahi hain. Agar aap sirf gusse ka ilaaj karte raho, to aap galat problem hi solve karte rahoge.

Sharir mein jagah dhoondho. Bhaari seena, garam chehra, kandhon ka bojh, pet jo shaant nahi hota. Sharir aksar dimaag ke maanne se pehle jaan leta hai, aur wahan se raasta zyada tez hai.

Ek line likho, nibandh nahi. Jo journal madad karta hai wo do page ki safai wala nahi hai. Wo yeh hai: aaj main zaroorat se zyada chidchida tha, aur shayad wo meeting ki wajah se tha.

Aur naam dena hi poora maqsad rehne do. Yeh feelings ko gayab karne ki technique nahi hai. Kuch ka rukna zaroori hota hai — gham ko hal nahi chahiye, jagah chahiye. Naam dena bas itna karta hai ki feelings parde ke peechhe se poora din chalana band kar deti hain — aur wahi version sabse mehnga padta hai.

articles.title: The Gap Between Reacting and Responding
articles.titleHinglish: React Karne Aur Jawab Dene Ke Beech Ka Gap
articles.content:
Someone says something sharp. Before you have decided anything, your reply is already out of your mouth, and it is worse than what they said. Ten minutes later you can think of four better things you could have done, all of them obvious.

The difference between reacting and responding is not intelligence or character. It is time. Reacting takes under a second. Responding needs somewhere between six seconds and six hours, and almost all of the skill is in creating that gap.

This is not about suppressing anger. Suppression is just a reaction that arrives later, usually at someone who did not earn it. The aim is to let the first surge pass so that what comes out is your decision rather than your chemistry.

A few reliable ways to build the gap.

Breathe out longer than you breathe in. Four counts in, six or eight out, three times. This is not mysticism — a long exhale is one of the few direct levers on the nervous system available to you. It brings the temperature down enough to think.

Move. Stand up, walk to the balcony, get a glass of water. Physical movement interrupts the loop, and the walk to the kitchen has saved more relationships than most advice.

Say the honest holding sentence. I want to answer this properly, give me some time. This is far better than silence, which is often read as punishment, and far better than the reply you would give right now.

And never send it hot. Write the message if you must — then keep it in drafts until morning. Almost nobody regrets waiting. Almost everybody regrets sending.

There is a second half to this that gets ignored. Responding well requires knowing what you actually want out of the exchange. Most heated replies are aimed at winning, and winning an argument with someone you have to live with is close to worthless. Ask: do I want them to understand me, to stop doing this, or to feel as bad as I do? The third one is honest and understandable, and it never produces anything you want to keep.

And be fair to yourself about the failures. You will react badly sometimes, especially when tired, hungry, or already stretched. The repair afterwards matters more than the record. I spoke badly earlier, that was not about you — said quickly and without a long defence — restores more than a perfect performance would have.
articles.contentHinglish:
Koi kuch teekha bol deta hai. Aapke kuch tay karne se pehle hi aapka jawab muh se nikal chuka hai, aur wo unki baat se bhi bura hai. Dus minute baad aapko chaar behtar jawab soojhte hain, aur sab obvious lagte hain.

React karne aur jawab dene mein farq buddhi ya charitra ka nahi hai. Farq waqt ka hai. React karne mein ek second se kam lagta hai. Jawab dene mein chhe second se chhe ghante lagte hain, aur poora hunar us gap ko banane mein hai.

Yeh gussa dabaane ki baat nahi hai. Dabaya hua gussa bhi ek reaction hi hai jo baad mein aata hai, aksar us par jisne kuch kiya hi nahi tha. Maqsad yeh hai ki pehli lehar guzar jaaye taaki jo bahar aaye wo aapka faisla ho, aapki chemistry nahi.

Gap banane ke kuch bharosemand tareeke.

Saans andar se zyada bahar chhodo. Chaar ginti andar, chhe ya aath bahar, teen baar. Yeh koi jaadu nahi — lambi saans chhodna un ginne-chune leverón mein se ek hai jo seedha nervous system par kaam karta hai. Wo temperature itna gira deta hai ki soch sako.

Hilo. Khade ho jao, balcony tak jao, paani ka glass lo. Sharir ka hilna loop todta hai, aur kitchen tak ki chaal ne zyadatar salaah se zyada rishte bachaye hain.

Wo imaandaar line bolo jo waqt maangti hai. Main iska theek se jawab dena chahta hoon, mujhe thoda waqt do. Yeh khamoshi se bahut behtar hai — khamoshi aksar sazaa samjhi jaati hai — aur us jawab se to bahut hi behtar hai jo aap abhi doge.

Aur garam mein kabhi mat bhejo. Message likh lo agar likhna hai — phir subah tak drafts mein rakho. Ruk jaane ka pachhtava lagbhag kisi ko nahi hota. Bhej dene ka lagbhag sabko hota hai.

Iska doosra hissa aksar chhoot jaata hai. Achha jawab dene ke liye pata hona chahiye ki aap is baat-cheet se chahte kya ho. Zyadatar garam jawab jeetne ke liye hote hain, aur jiske saath rehna hai usse bahas jeetna lagbhag bekaar hai. Poochho: main chahta hoon ki wo mujhe samjhein, ki wo yeh karna band karein, ya ki unhe bhi utna hi bura lage jitna mujhe? Teesri baat imaandaar aur samajh mein aane wali hai, aur usse kabhi kuch aisa nahi milta jise aap rakhna chahoge.

Aur apni galtiyon par khud ke saath insaaf rakho. Kabhi kabhi aap bura react karoge — khaaskar jab thake, bhookhe ya pehle se khinche hue ho. Uske baad ki marammat record se zyada mayne rakhti hai. "Maine pehle galat bola, wo tumhare baare mein nahi tha" — jaldi aur bina lambi safai ke — wo perfect performance se zyada wapas jodta hai.

articles.title: You Are Allowed to Feel Two Things at Once
articles.titleHinglish: Ek Saath Do Cheezein Mehsoos Karna Allowed Hai
articles.content:
You can be relieved that it ended and devastated that it ended. Proud of your friend and jealous of him. Grateful to your parents and angry at them. Most people believe one of these has to be false, so they spend enormous energy deciding which feeling is the real one.

Both are real. Emotions do not run on a single track, and the demand for consistency is something we impose afterwards, usually because a mixed feeling is harder to explain to other people.

This matters practically, because the effort to feel only one approved emotion causes more damage than the emotions themselves.

Take grief. People who lose someone after a long illness often feel relief, and then feel monstrous for feeling it. The relief is not a betrayal of love. It is the end of exhaustion and helplessness, sitting right beside the loss. Denying it does not remove it; it just adds shame on top of grief.

Or gratitude and anger toward family. In Indian homes especially, many people believe that acknowledging what their parents got wrong would cancel everything they got right. So they pick one — either the full obedience of they did everything for me, or the full rejection of they ruined me. Both versions are simplifications, and neither leaves room for an actual adult relationship. They loved you, they did their best with what they had, and some of what they did hurt you and still affects how you behave at thirty. All of that, at once, is closer to the truth than any single clean sentence.

The practice is small. When you notice yourself asking which feeling is the real one, replace the question with the word and. I am relieved and I am heartbroken. I am proud of him and I wish it had been me. I love them and I am still angry about that year.

Saying it that way does something specific. It stops the internal argument, which is the part that consumes the energy. You are no longer prosecuting yourself for having a contradiction; you are simply holding two facts.

And it makes you easier to be around. People who have to resolve every feeling into a single verdict end up performing — cheerful when they are not, forgiving before they mean it, or hardened past what they actually feel. Someone who can say I am happy for you and it is hard to hear this today is telling the truth, and the truth, mixed as it is, is usually what other people can actually work with.
articles.contentHinglish:
Aap raahat bhi mehsoos kar sakte ho ki khatam ho gaya aur toot bhi sakte ho ki khatam ho gaya. Dost par garv bhi kar sakte ho aur jalan bhi. Maa-baap ke shukraguzaar bhi ho sakte ho aur unpar gussa bhi. Zyadatar log maante hain ki inme se ek jhoothi honi chahiye, isliye wo bahut saari energy yeh tay karne mein lagate hain ki asli feeling kaunsi hai.

Dono asli hain. Emotions ek hi patri par nahi chalte, aur consistency ki maang hum baad mein thopte hain — aksar isliye ki mili-juli feeling doosron ko samjhaana mushkil hota hai.

Yeh practically mayne rakhta hai, kyunki sirf ek "manzoor shuda" emotion mehsoos karne ki koshish khud un emotions se zyada nuksaan karti hai.

Gham ko lo. Lambi bimaari ke baad kisi ko khone par logon ko aksar raahat mehsoos hoti hai, aur phir wo khud ko rakshas samajhte hain. Wo raahat pyaar ke saath gaddaari nahi hai. Wo thakan aur bebasi ka ant hai, jo nuksaan ke bilkul bagal mein baitha hai. Use jhutlaane se wo hatti nahi; bas gham ke upar sharm chadh jaati hai.

Ya parivaar ke liye shukraguzaari aur gussa. Khaaskar Indian gharon mein, bahut se log maante hain ki maa-baap ne jo galat kiya use maan lena unke sahi kiye hue sab kuch ko kaat dega. Isliye wo ek chunte hain — ya to poora aagyapaalan "unhone mere liye sab kiya", ya poora inkaar "unhone mujhe barbaad kiya". Dono version simplification hain, aur kisi mein bhi ek asli, badon wale rishte ki jagah nahi bachti. Unhone aapse pyaar kiya, jo unke paas tha usme apna best diya, aur unme se kuch ne aapko chot pahunchayi jo aaj tees ki umar mein bhi asar karti hai. Yeh sab ek saath sach ke zyada kareeb hai bajaye kisi ek saaf sentence ke.

Practice chhoti hai. Jab khud ko yeh poochhte pakdo ki asli feeling kaunsi hai, sawaal ki jagah "aur" shabd rakh do. Mujhe raahat hai aur mera dil toota hua hai. Mujhe uspar garv hai aur kaash yeh main hota. Main unse pyaar karta hoon aur us saal ko lekar abhi bhi gussa hoon.

Aise bolne se ek khaas cheez hoti hai. Andar ki bahas ruk jaati hai, aur energy wahi bahas khaati hai. Ab aap khud par contradiction rakhne ka mukadma nahi chala rahe; aap bas do facts pakde hue ho.

Aur isse aapke saath rehna aasaan ho jaata hai. Jo log har feeling ko ek hi faisle mein badalna chahte hain, wo performance karne lagte hain — bina khush hue khush, mann se pehle maafi, ya jitni sakhti asli hai usse zyada sakhti. Jo insaan bol sakta hai "main tumhare liye khush hoon aur aaj yeh sunna mushkil hai" — wo sach bol raha hai, aur mila-jula sach hi wo cheez hai jiske saath doosre log sach mein kuch kar sakte hain.
